Card status block.copy: Keeps status, limit, risk, and usable balance visible before card-level actions.

Quick actions.copy: Groups frequent controls while preserving confirmation, disabled reasons, and support routing.

Movement receipt detail.copy: Explains a movement with merchant, amount, authorization, timestamp, card, and support evidence.

Dispute entry point.copy: Starts recovery with eligibility, required evidence, expected timing, and audit trail.

Driver Card Wallet.standard: This template is the card-control workspace: it must keep status, limits, movements, quick actions, and dispute recovery in one accountable system.
Driver Card Wallet.screenSystem: The screen system separates card state, actions, movement evidence, and support entry so each module can fail or recover without hiding the card context.
Driver Card Wallet.informationArchitecture: Navigation follows the wallet mental model: card first, movements second, limits third, help always available.
Driver Card Wallet.primary: Driver needs fast control over a payment card while understanding risk, limits, support, and movement history.
qualityGates: Card status and limits remain visible before quick actions.
Movement detail includes merchant, amount, authorization, and support route.
Blocked or risky states explain the next safe action.

templateModuleDetails.Mobile Card Overview: Keeps status, limit, movement summary, blocked states, and next useful action visible.
templateModuleDetails.Mobile Card Detail and Quick Actions: Lets drivers control a card while preserving confirmation, disabled reasons, and support handoff.
templateModuleDetails.Mobile Movement Detail: Turns each movement into receipt-like evidence with recovery, dispute, and audit context.

Map with station pins.copy: Shows nearby stations with permission, loading, cluster, and selected-pin states.

Fallback station list.copy: Keeps station discovery usable when map, GPS, or network context is unavailable.

Station services panel.copy: Compares service availability, distance, fuel types, schedule, and restrictions.

Route handoff.copy: Transfers station context to navigation while preserving ETA, destination, and recovery copy.

Routes and Stations.standard: This template is the station-discovery workspace: map, list, station detail, and route handoff must stay equivalent, especially when location or network context fails.
Routes and Stations.screenSystem: The screen system keeps map and list as parallel paths, with station detail and navigation handoff as explicit decisions.
Routes and Stations.informationArchitecture: Navigation follows travel intent: discover, compare, inspect, and route.
Routes and Stations.primary: Driver searches nearby stations, compares useful station information, and starts navigation with graceful location fallback.
qualityGates: Map and list remain equivalent paths.
Location denial shows fallback list and manual station search.
Route handoff preserves station context and recovery copy.

patternDetails.Station Discovery: Owns map pins, fallback list equivalence, permission recovery, selected station state, provider readiness, and route handoff for the route workspace.

templateModuleDetails.Routes and Nearby Stations Mobile: Keeps map, list, permissions, distance, and selected station in the same decision path.
templateModuleDetails.Station Detail and Route Guidance: Moves from station comparison to external navigation with ETA, service restrictions, and recovery.
